decision: Entry-relative tables regress the new computed-arm dispatch kernel by about 5%. The simpler table-base-relative layout is closer but has no measured gain (default 1.022, release 1.009, both inconclusive). No full suite or full stage gate was run; retain the new benchmark and behavioral tests instead.

relative-tables.patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/x64.jo b/core/compiler/x64.jo
index ef02a939..41a6937f 100644
--- a/core/compiler/x64.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/x64.jo
@@ -2377,15 +2377,29 @@ emit_ins = (pos: int, ins: Ins):
                 modrr(ra, ra)
                 branch_target_jcc(int(ins.imm), CC_NE)
         brtable:
-            # bounds check, then jump into a table of 5-byte jmp instructions
+            # Signed offsets relative to the end of each four-byte entry.
+            # Existing block fixups can patch these exactly like rel32 jumps;
+            # dispatch reaches the arm directly rather than another jump.
             ld(RAX, a)
             b(0x48); b(0x81); modrr(7, RAX); b32(bb)          # cmp rax, n
             branch_target_jcc(int(ins.imm), CC_AE)
-            b(0x48); b(0x8D); b(0x0C); b(0x80)                # lea rcx, [rax + rax*4]
-            b(0x48); b(0x8D); b(0x05); b32(5)                 # lea rax, [rip + 5]
-            b(0x48); b(0x01); b(0xC8)                         # add rax, rcx
+            b(0x48); b(0x8D); b(0x0D); b32(0)                 # lea rcx, [rip + table]
+            table_fix = code.len() - 4
+            use_index(RAX, 2)
+            lea(RAX, RCX, 0)                                 # address of the selected entry
+            cur_index = -1
+            load_sized(RCX, RAX, 0, 4, true)                  # signed arm offset
+            use_index(RCX, 0)
+            lea(RAX, RAX, 4)                                 # entry + 4 + offset
+            cur_index = -1
             b(0xFF); b(0xE0)                                  # jmp rax
-            loop k in [0..bb): branch_target_fix(int(ir.args[int(ins.c) + k]))
+            patch_here(table_fix)
+            loop k in [0..bb):
+                target = xctl.len() - 1 - int(ir.args[int(ins.c) + k])
+                if xctl[target].kind == 1: b32(xctl[target].start - (code.len() + 4))
+                else:
+                    xctl[target].fixups.push(code.len())
+                    b32(0)
         ret:
             if a >= 0:
                 ty = vtype(a)

base-tables.patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/x64.jo b/core/compiler/x64.jo
index ef02a939..1494f7e4 100644
--- a/core/compiler/x64.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/x64.jo
@@ -1119,6 +1119,7 @@ struct XCtl:
     start: int
     fixups: int[]
     ifx: int[]    # jumps to the else branch
+    table_fixups: (int, int)[]  # entry position, table base
 
 xctl: XCtl[]
 call_stack_bytes = 0
@@ -2326,14 +2327,14 @@ emit_ins = (pos: int, ins: Ins):
                 stub_fix.push((code.len() - 4, int(ins.imm)))
                 pop_call_stack()
                 if d >= 0 and vloc[d] != LOC_NONE: st(d, RAX)
-        block: xctl.push(XCtl(0, code.len(), [], []))
+        block: xctl.push(XCtl(0, code.len(), [], [], []))
         loop:
             # Default code needs a consistent loop entry before comparison
             # padding. Release keeps its measured limited-padding policy.
             if ra_on:
                 if not opt_release or (16 - code.len() % 16) % 16 <= 10: nop_pad((16 - code.len() % 16) % 16)
                 else: nop_pad((8 - code.len() % 8) % 8)
-            xctl.push(XCtl(1, code.len(), [], []))
+            xctl.push(XCtl(1, code.len(), [], [], []))
         if_:
             fx: int[]
             if fused_cc >= 0:
@@ -2346,7 +2347,7 @@ emit_ins = (pos: int, ins: Ins):
                 b(0x85)
                 modrr(ra, ra)                   # test r, r
                 fx.push(jcc32(CC_E))
-            xctl.push(XCtl(2, code.len(), [], fx))
+            xctl.push(XCtl(2, code.len(), [], fx, []))
         else_:
             c = xctl.len() - 1
             xctl[c].fixups.push(jmp32())
@@ -2356,6 +2357,7 @@ emit_ins = (pos: int, ins: Ins):
             c = xctl.pop()
             loop f in c.fixups: patch_here(f)
             loop f in c.ifx: patch_here(f)
+            loop f in c.table_fixups: patch32(f.0, code.len() - f.1)
         br: branch_target_fix(int(ins.imm))
         brif:
             if fused_cc >= 0:
@@ -2377,15 +2379,26 @@ emit_ins = (pos: int, ins: Ins):
                 modrr(ra, ra)
                 branch_target_jcc(int(ins.imm), CC_NE)
         brtable:
-            # bounds check, then jump into a table of 5-byte jmp instructions
+            # Four-byte signed offsets from the table base. One indirect
+            # branch reaches the arm directly rather than another jump.
             ld(RAX, a)
             b(0x48); b(0x81); modrr(7, RAX); b32(bb)          # cmp rax, n
             branch_target_jcc(int(ins.imm), CC_AE)
-            b(0x48); b(0x8D); b(0x0C); b(0x80)                # lea rcx, [rax + rax*4]
-            b(0x48); b(0x8D); b(0x05); b32(5)                 # lea rax, [rip + 5]
-            b(0x48); b(0x01); b(0xC8)                         # add rax, rcx
+            b(0x48); b(0x8D); b(0x0D); b32(0)                 # lea rcx, [rip + table]
+            table_fix = code.len() - 4
+            use_index(RAX, 2)
+            load_sized(RAX, RCX, 0, 4, true)                  # signed arm offset
+            cur_index = -1
+            op_rr(0x01, true, RCX, RAX)                       # add rax, rcx (table base)
             b(0xFF); b(0xE0)                                  # jmp rax
-            loop k in [0..bb): branch_target_fix(int(ir.args[int(ins.c) + k]))
+            patch_here(table_fix)
+            table_base = code.len()
+            loop k in [0..bb):
+                target = xctl.len() - 1 - int(ir.args[int(ins.c) + k])
+                if xctl[target].kind == 1: b32(xctl[target].start - table_base)
+                else:
+                    xctl[target].table_fixups.push((code.len(), table_base))
+                    b32(0)
         ret:
             if a >= 0:
                 ty = vtype(a)

benchmark.name: branch_dispatch
benchmark.reason: Existing match_dispatch optimizes into a constant-result lookup and does not exercise branch-table dispatch. This separate workload has varying operands and computed arms.
benchmark.oracle: Independent Python arithmetic at 1000 iterations, plus matching C results at 0, 1, 17, 1000 and full count in both pilots.
